chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mu'tamir (one who performs Umrah after Hajj). He said, 'When the comb can reach his head, it is good.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shaving the head after performing Umrah following Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ritual completion of Ihram for a Mutamatti' pilgrim by linking the permissibility of grooming to the physical act of hair removal, specifically shaving or trimming. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the significance of 'Tahallul' (release from Ihram restrictions), where the ability to comb hair signifies the transition from the sacred state to ordinary status, emphasizing the practical ease granted to pilgrims after fulfilling their obligations.
